parsed.reason: The reply ends by asking the parent to reply YES to get "the full plan" — but YES is the confirmation trigger reserved for schedule changes, not a gating mechanism for advice. This inverts the product contract and withholds the actionable guidance behind an extra round-trip. The parent asked a parenting question and the reply gives only orientation (6-month window, three signs to watch) without the concrete thing they could do now. Worse, the offer to send "the full plan" on YES turns Hale's own machinery into the subject of the message, which is self-absorbed. A 5 would have delivered the watch-for signs and one concrete next step (e.g., "when he hits 6 months try a small spoonful of single-grain cereal or purée once a day") in the space available.
